scoring_justification: Spectral efficiency is recomputed from the agent's raw reflectance spectra using Planck integration at 1750 K and GaSb bandgap 0.726 eV. The recomputed efficiencies are compared to the paper's reported values (0.59 and 0.70) with monotonic, threshold-or-better scoring. This is T1 recompute because both reflectance artifacts are raw outputs of the FDTD simulation and we numerically integrate them to get the final metric, independent of any agent-reported number.

outputs.description: Reflectance spectrum of the blazed grating without back reflector, used to compute spectral efficiency.
Reflectance spectrum of the blazed grating with a perfect back reflector, used to compute spectral efficiency.

output_contract.notes: The hidden checker will recompute spectral efficiency from each reflectance spectrum using Eq. (1) (Planck's law at 1750 K, GaSb bandgap 0.726 eV) and compare against threshold_or_better criteria.

hidden_assets.purpose: Gold spectral efficiency values for blazed grating without and with back reflector
hidden_assets.source_provenance: Paper: the optimized blazed grating (period 200 nm, height 285 nm, blaze angle 55°) achieves a spectral efficiency of 0.59 without back reflector and 0.70 with back reflector, as reported in the abstract, Table 1, and Figs. 3-4.
hidden_assets.generation_method: Copied from the paper's reported values.
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: These are the paper's main numerical result and are publicly known; using them as reference thresholds is legitimate.
